recipes.name: Basic Bread Pudding II
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 pound) loaf white bread, torn into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a large mixing bowl, pour hot milk over bread. Blend eggs, sugar, and vanilla. Stir egg mixture into the bread mixture and blend well. Add raisins. Mix well.
Melt the margarine and pour into a 9x13-inch pan. Pour bread mixture over margarine. Bake for 40 minutes, or until firm and golden brown. Serve hot or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Basic Bread Pudding II
raw_recipe.description: This bread pudding is very versatile and lovely in texture. Christmas time can inspire a bread pudding by simply substituting a good-quality eggnog for the milk (or part of it). Also add a pinch of nutmeg and mace to produce a sumptuous holiday dessert. Otherwise, enjoy this just as it is with a dollop of whipped cream.

review.reviewBody:
VERY GOOD!! My entire family LOVED it!! Everyone was eating seconds. I used cinnamon raisin bread and regular bread. I also added a little more raisins, nutmeg and cinnamon. Also 1/2 eggnog and 1/2 milk. I used this simple recipe for vanilla sauce...
Serve this vanilla sauce with bread pudding or any other dessert. 
INGREDIENTS:

1/2 cup sugar 
1 tablespoon cornstarch 
1 cup boiling water
2 tablespoons butter
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
dash salt
PREPARATION:

In small saucepan combine sugar and cornstarch. Stir in 1 cup boiling water. Simmer, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tablespoons butter, vanilla extract and salt; blend well. 
Thank you for such a great addition to my Christmas dinner!!!

It was very good. I toasted the bread before cutting it into pieces and added a few ingredients- cinnamon, nutmeg, a pinch of salt, and 1/8 cup packed brown sugar. I cooked it covered in in a water bath about 35 minutes longer than recommended. Gently stir when pudding begins to set (just enough to mix a bit) before serving. Serve with whip cream or ice cream.

I followed the basic recipe except I made a few changes. I used a 26.4 ounce pumpkin panettone that I cut up and let dry out all day and added about 2 teaspoons of pie spice to the sugar mixture and 1 cup of chocolate chips instead of the raisins. I put this into 2 8x8 pans so I have 1 for the family on Thanksgiving and 1 for my family after. I did follow the baking instructions and they came out perfectly.

DELICIOUS! I was a huge hit at our church dinner! I skipped the raisins, used half and half instead of milk, added 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg and a teaspoon cinnamon. I mixed the eggs, half and half, sugar and spices together and poured over the bread. I served with a simple butterscotch sauce made with brown sugar, butter, milk, and corn syrup. Will definitely make it again!

This was the first time I’ve ever made bread pudding. It was delicious! I used the sweet Easter bread I had just made. I drizzled the butter over the bread and used cold milk. I mixed milk, eggs, sugar, vanilla and cinnamon and poured it over the bread. I won’t be afraid to make bread pudding ever again. This recipe is a keeper.

I used St Pierre brand sliced brioche bread and it was amazingly delicious. Had about 1 cup of heavy whipping cream in the fridge so substituted it for half of the whole milk. Will make again.- and soon!

FANTASTIC!! I made this for breakfast this morning. Who said bread pudding can only be earen for dessert. I used Pepperidge Farm Cinnamon Raisin Bread, so I didn'g add raisins. I only used 1/2 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar, as 2 cups of sugar sounded way too sweet. I beat together the milk (not hot), eggs, sugars, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg, and then poured that over the torn bread. I let that stand for 15 minutes or so and then poured it into the pan with melted butter and baked it. I just seemed easier that way. This is the best bread pudding I've ever made! Be adventurous and try it for breakfast!

I followed the recipe with just a few suggestions incorporated. I did cut back on the sugar. Used a cup of white and 1/4 of brown. BUT also added about 1 1/2 cups of caramel macchiato creamer, 1 1/2 cups of half and half and the balance of the quart of milk (went a little over a quart) with skim milk. Spiced it up with approximately a teaspoon of cinnamon and a half teaspoon of nutmeg. Didn't heat the milk but also took the suggestion of adding all the liquids, sugar, eggs and spices and whisked together. Poured over the bread pieces and let sit for about 15 min before putting in the pan and baking. As we like to say, it turned out so good it is worthy of the next month of church potlucks.

Great to find more recipes that give a mass of bread instead of "slices." This recipe needs spices - I found that 1 T. true cinnamon and 1 t. fresh ground nutmeg gives it enough. Also, you can cut the sugar down to 1 c. and it is still plenty.
Was delicious! I tweaked it by using brown sugar instead of white and melted some brown sugar with butter and poured that on top to make a nice glaze.

Instead of raisins, I used a cup of triple berry blend (dried cherries, blueberries, and cranberries) and cooked them in a bit of rum until the alcohol cooked off and the berries were nice and plump. So delicious! Will definitely use this recipe again!
It was good, I'll try it again with tweets.

I tried this for myself a couple of weeks ago and liked how easy it was to make and how good it tasted! We had a bridge tournament at our club this weekend and I made it for that. I've never had so many compliments on anything I've made (I'm culinarily impaired)! Several people asked me for the recipe too! I'm not a raisin fan, so I substituted blueberries which was perfect.
It is so easy and GOOOOD!! Made it with whiskey sauce......WOW!!

I’ve made bread pudding all my life, but it’s been awhile since I have. Thought I’d get a refresher. Sounds like I do it except for the 2 cups of sugar. Anyone else think this is excessive. I’ll try with just a cup and more spices, might even add a little apple to it.
Just like mom used to make
I used day old cinnamon rolls with icing and cut the sugar down to 3/4 of a cup and added peaches. Yum!
